transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~40 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Rajiv Menon (CTO, Orion Newco), Maya Li (Dev Lead), Omar Khalid (Security)

Summary:
Short discovery focused on PLG/self-serve Redwood API quickstart, free credits/time-to-first-token, and initial fit for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Security concerns raised around KMS and audit logs, plus timeline for a small pilot.

Topics:
- Quickstart and free credits
- Time-to-first-token and SDK experience
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
- Security/compliance (KMS, audit logs, data residency)
- Next steps and pilot plan

Transcript (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect in places):
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone—thanks for joining. I'm Avery, AE on the Redwood team, and with me is Sofia, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Rajiv Menon: Good, thanks. Quick note, we only have about 40 minutes, so we'll focus on our main questions: quickstart, cost, and security.
[00:20] Sofia Patel: Totally, we'll keep it tight. Can I do a 30-second state check on your stack? What's your current setup for embeddings and generation?
[00:30] Maya Li: Sure. We're a small infra team—primarily using a mix: embeddings in-house for search (we store vectors in Postgres + Faiss), generation currently via a prototype using public LLMs, plus some on-prem models for PII-sensitive flows.
[00:45] Omar Khalid: Security is our main blocker for any hosted service — we need KMS integration, audit logs, and clear retention.
[00:52] Avery Chen: Understood. The quickstart is really PLG/self-serve: signup, free credits, and a few lines of code to get first token streaming. For Hosted you can be up in minutes; Dedicated or Private we'd scope for enterprise.
[01:10] Rajiv Menon: When you say "minutes", do you mean our engineers can demo generation in an hour? We want to validate latency and cost quickly.
[01:18] Sofia Patel: Yes — time-to-first-token for basic tests is commonly under 10 minutes from signup for the Redwood API. We'll send sample cURL and SDK snippets. For a perf benchmark we'll schedule a dedicated SE session.
[01:30] Maya Li: And the free credits — what's the size and expiration?
[01:35] Avery Chen: We typically provide an initial credit bundle for quickstarts — we can do 1,000 free credit units (we'll describe units in the email) valid for 30 days for trial accounts. For pilots we can expand that.
[01:46] Rajiv Menon: Sounds good. I want to understand Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private: for our use-case, we care about latency and data isolation.
[01:55] Sofia Patel: Great question. Hosted is our managed API — fastest to get started, cost-efficient for lower compliance needs. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictability — good if you need consistent throughput and some data isolation. Private (VPC/on-prem) is for regulated or air-gapped needs: you run control plane privately and we support KMS/HSM integrations.
[02:20] Omar Khalid: For security: can you outline encryption at-rest and key management? We need to tie into our AWS KMS or a customer HSM.
[02:30] Avery Chen: Yes — Hosted supports customer-managed keys via KMS integration for enterprise tiers, and Private supports HSM/KMS. We'll share the security pack. Audit logs and RBAC are available in enterprise plans.
[02:44] Maya Li: Any SOC/ISO certifications?
[02:47] Sofia Patel: We have SOC 2 info and are ISO-aligned — will send the certs in the security pack.
[02:55] Rajiv Menon: Performance wise — can we run a short benchmark to compare a 4k-token prompt on Hosted vs Dedicated? 
[03:05] Sofia Patel: Absolutely. For the pilot we typically do: 1) sample dataset, 2) defined prompt sets, 3) run 30-60 minute load tests to measure p95 latency and tokens/sec. We can mirror your sequence lengths.
[03:18] Rajiv Menon: What's the usual p95 on Hosted for, say, a 2k token generation?
[03:25] Sofia Patel: Ballpark depends on model selection. If you pick a smaller open model we can see low-latency. For larger LLMs and longer sequences, Dedicated gives more predictable p95 because of reserved capacity. We'll give you benchmark sheets.
[03:39] Omar Khalid: Any data residency options? We operate mostly in EU regions and need logs stored in region.
[03:46] Avery Chen: Yes — region pinning is possible for Dedicated and Private; Hosted has region options too in our EU region. We'll clarify data residency in the security docs.
[03:57] Maya Li: I have a dev question: SDKs — do you support Node and Python streaming out of box?
[04:03] Sofia Patel: Yes — official SDKs for Python and Node with streaming and function-calling support. Quickstart includes a sample app.
[04:12] Rajiv Menon: Ok, walk me through what we'd need to do to get a quick proof in 1 week.
[04:17] Avery Chen: Steps: 1) sign up and redeem free credits, 2) run quickstart sample to get first token, 3) share sample dataset with us, 4) schedule a 1-hour SE perf session. We can get you to a basic proof-of-concept in a few days depending on availability.
[04:32] Maya Li: On the sign-up — does the account require company SSO or can we create trial accounts?
[04:37] Avery Chen: Trial accounts are self-serve; enterprise onboarding with SSO/SAML is optional for pilots or later.
[04:45] Rajiv Menon: Cost model — how granular is the cost? Per token? Any minimum commit?
[04:50] Sofia Patel: Hosted is usage-based (per-token/per-embedding). Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits. We'll share a pricing sketch but for a small pilot Hosted usage is easiest.
[05:02] Omar Khalid: A security nit — how long do you retain request logs and how are they exposed?
[05:09] Avery Chen: Logs retention depends on plan; audit logs available for enterprise customers and can be exported to your SIEM; default retention is shorter for Hosted but configurable for Dedicated/Private. We'll include the exact retention matrix.
[05:23] Rajiv Menon: Any customers doing a similar hybrid setup—embeddings in house, generation hosted?
[05:29] Sofia Patel: Yeah, many customers keep embeddings or vector stores on-prem (for e.g., Faiss, Postgres) while using Hosted for generation calls. We're designed for that mixed topology.
[05:40] Maya Li: About model variants — if capacity is constrained do you do automated fallback to smaller models?
[05:46] Sofia Patel: Yes — smart routing and fallback policies exist; you can configure fallbacks by latency or cost constraints.
[05:54] Rajiv Menon: For the pilot we want to validate both functional quality and unit economics. Can we get a recommended quantization/instance mix?
[06:03] Sofia Patel: We'll provide model/quant recommendation based on your prompt lengths and QPS. That's part of Redwood Optimize — we'll propose batching and quant profiles.
[06:14] Rajiv Menon: Great. Any concerns we should flag internally before the pilot?
[06:18] Avery Chen: Main points: define success criteria (latency target, cost per 1k tokens, quality metrics), provide sample prompt sets, and choose models to test.
[06:28] Maya Li: I'm worried about noisy transcription here— sorry I mean noisy network, but also our team wants deterministic outputs for some flows. How do you handle model versioning and rollbacks?
[06:39] Sofia Patel: Model pinning and rollouts are available— you can pin a model version and do canary rollouts with automatic fallback. We also support structured evals to detect regressions.
[06:50] Rajiv Menon: Any mention of competitors? We evaluated OpenAI for simplicity but worried about vendor lock; looked at Vertex for infra integration.
[06:58] Avery Chen: We hear that a lot — Redwood's edge is unified serving across Hosted/Dedicated/Private and explicit cost/perf controls.
[07:06] Maya Li: For the quickstart, what is the SDK snippet — can you paste a short one in the follow-up?
[07:10] Sofia Patel: Yes — we'll include Node/Python snippets and a sample streaming demo.
[07:15] Rajiv Menon: Ok let's get more specific on timeline. If we sign up this week, when can we run benchmarks?
[07:20] Avery Chen: If you sign up and share your dataset by end of the week, we can kick off a bench the following week — Sofia will coordinate times.
[07:27] Maya Li: Omar, any final security questions?
[07:31] Omar Khalid: Not final but I need to review the KMS integration guide and any SOC/ISO docs— plus proof of export controls if we move data across regions.
[07:39] Avery Chen: We'll send the security pack and add you to the pilot thread.
[07:45] Rajiv Menon: Sounds good. One last question about cost visibility — does your console show token-level breakdowns per API key?
[07:52] Sofia Patel: Yes — Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route/model and you can tag keys to map to teams.
[07:59] Maya Li: Nice. Any sticky points if we start on Hosted and later move to Dedicated? Data migration?
[08:05] Sofia Patel: We try to make it seamless; you can pin model versions and we support snapshotting configs. There is some onboarding for Dedicated (capacity sizing), but migration paths are standard.
[08:16] Rajiv Menon: Ok let's wrap. Can you recap next steps?
[08:19] Avery Chen: Sure — recap: 1) I'll send the quickstart link + free credit code + SDK snippets (Avery). 2) Sofia will draft pilot benchmark plan and rough cost estimate. 3) Rajiv/Maya share sample dataset and KPIs. 4) Send security pack to Omar. We'll aim to have the initial pilot scheduled week of 2026-03-09.
[08:41] Maya Li: Thanks — that's great.
[08:43] Rajiv Menon: Thanks all.
[08:45] Avery Chen: Appreciate your time — we'll follow up via email with links and schedule.

End of transcript.
